chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: Abu Muhammad al-Ghiffari narrated to me from Lut ibn Ishaq, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant who brings joy to a believing family, except that Allah creates for him from that joy a creature that will come to him on the Day of Judgment. Whenever a hardship passes over him, it will say: O beloved of Allah, do not fear. He will ask it: May Allah have mercy on you, who are you? It will say: I am the joy that you brought to the family of so-and-so.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for making a believing family happy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq narrates this hadith via a chain reaching back to Imam al-Sadiq (or the Prophet), emphasizing the metaphysical reality of 'joy' as a tangible intercessor on the Day of Judgment. This entity, created from the specific act of bringing happiness to a believer's family, serves as a personal comforter during the trials of the Hereafter, illustrating the Shia concept of deeds manifesting as distinct spiritual entities. The narration highlights the enduring value of social kindness (mu'amalat) as a source of divine protection and reassurance.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  The  Holy  Prophet  (s.a.w.s.)  said,  “One  who  makes  a believing family pleased, the Almighty Allah would make a creature out of those pleasures on the Day of Judgment. It will come to that person whenever he is in some problem. It will help him and say, ‘O lover of Allah! Do not fear’. He will ask, ‘May Allah’s mercy be upon you, who are you? If I would  have  owned  the  whole  world  then  too  it  had  no comparison with you’. It will reply, ‘I am the happiness you gave to such and such family’.”
